scenes.heading: How does the water cycle work?
scenes.subtitle: Water keeps moving around our planet
scenes.narration: The water on Earth moves in a never-ending loop called the water cycle.

scenes.heading: Four steps that repeat
scenes.narration: The cycle has four main steps that repeat again and again.

steps.narration: First, the sun heats water in seas and lakes, and it rises as water vapour.
High in the sky, the vapour cools into tiny droplets that form clouds.
When the droplets join and grow heavy, they fall as rain, snow or hail.
The water collects in rivers, lakes, seas and the ground, and the cycle starts again.
Most of Earth's water is in the oceans and seas, and it is salty.
Much of the fresh water is frozen in ice caps and glaciers.
Some water is stored under the ground, as groundwater.
Lakes and rivers hold only a tiny part of it.

steps.text: The sun powers the water cycle
steps.narration: The sun's heat drives the whole water cycle.
The four steps are evaporation, condensation, precipitation and collection.
Earth keeps reusing the same water, again and again.
